findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body:
`queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain default value. Python evaluates it once, when the class is defined at module import. Every `AssignmentSource` created afterwards (e.g. via `from_integration`) carries the same timestamp: the moment the worker process started, not when the assignment was queued.

Any later logic or debugging that relies on `queued` will be wrong, often by hours or days. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: Task kwargs contain a raw datetime that won't survive JSON serialization
findings.body:
`assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, so the `queued` field stays a `datetime` object. That dict is passed straight into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`.

Sentry's task kwargs are expected to be JSON-serializable. A raw `datetime` either fails or triggers serialization warnings/errors. If it is coerced to a string, `from_dict` rebuilds the dataclass with `queued` as a `str`, silently breaking the declared type.

This matters most on the inbound-webhook path, which is the exact path the PR is meant to protect. Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. `isoformat()` or a timestamp) in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` param on `sync_status_outbound` is never passed
findings.body:
The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature now takes `assignment_source`, but no caller in this PR passes it. Status-sync loops are therefore not addressed, despite the API suggesting otherwise.

The parameter is also named for assignment, which is confusing on a status-sync method. Either wire it through for status changes or drop it to avoid a misleading interface.
